Earnings Call Transcript
Sify (SIFY) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Apr 13, 2026 at 3:42PM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


DATE
Monday, April 13, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
Chairman — Raju Vegesna
Executive Director and Group CFO — M. P. Vijay Kumar
Vice President, Investor Relations — Praveen Krishna
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
TAKEAWAYS
Revenue
-- INR 4,487 million, representing a 13% increase.
EBITDA
-- INR 9,871 million, an increase of 31%.
Loss Before Tax
-- INR 941 million.
Loss After Tax
-- INR 1,366 million.
Cash Balance
-- INR 5,071 million at fiscal year-end.
Capital Expenditure
-- INR 13,282 million for the year, with management guiding for significantly higher CapEx in the upcoming fiscal year due to planned capacity expansion.
Revenue by Segment
-- Network Services: 39%, Data Center Services: 3%, Digital Services: 22%
Segment Revenue Growth
-- Network Services up 12%, Data Center Services up 23%, Digital Services down 2%.
Segment Results Growth
-- Network Services results up 91%, Data Center Colocation results up 24%, Digital Services results down 67%.
Data Center Capacity
-- 188 megawatts total design capacity, with 129 megawatts revenue-generating as of March 26.
Data Center Backlog
-- 81 megawatts contracted for future delivery, scheduled to be delivered in phases within the current fiscal year.
Installed Data Center Capacity
-- 140 megawatts as of March 26 (previously 127 megawatts as of prior year).
Data Center Operational Capacity
-- 129 megawatts as of March 26 (previously 111 megawatts as of prior year).
Network Services Coverage
-- 1,224 fiber nodes deployed, an 8% increase.
SDWAN Service Points
-- 10,340 active across India.
Planned Expansion
-- Management to nearly double revenue-generating data center capacity over the next year.
IPO Details for Sify Infinite Space
-- INR 2,500 crores primary, INR 1,200 crores offer for sale, INR 3,700 crores total size; all regulatory approvals received, timing to be determined with bankers.
Government Incentive
-- Chairman Raju Vegesna noted a newly introduced 20-year tax holiday for foreign cloud service providers using Indian data centers for global services.
Data Center Development
-- Ongoing construction of two major expansions at Rabale: one at 77 megawatts and another at 52 megawatts, both designed with potential for additional scaling.
Margin Guidance
-- Management targets breakeven in the data center services segment within two years, with “quarterly improvement going forward.”
CapEx Drivers
-- Anticipated CapEx increase attributed to nearly doubling of revenue-generating data center capacity.
Demand Shifts
-- M. P. Vijay Kumar stated, “We are seeing that happen for our data center collection business and consequently, to our network business as well,” regarding increased demand from Middle East client interactions.
Segment Growth Outlook
-- Network Services growing at low double-digit rates; Digital Services continues investment in AI infrastructure.
Data Center EBITDA Potential
-- Management indicates liquid cooling may lead to higher EBITDA per megawatt, but specifics depend on contract structures.
No Significant Rollout Bottlenecks
-- Management states current construction faces no material supply chain or energy availability issues, citing strong government support.
SUMMARY
Management communicated targeted expansion with nearly doubled revenue-generating data center capacity planned within the fiscal year, driving an expected material increase in capital expenditures. The company confirmed all regulatory approvals for the Sify Infinite Space IPO, totaling INR 3,700 crores, with launch timing pending banker guidance. Representatives highlighted continued government support, including a new 20-year tax holiday for qualifying foreign cloud customers. Operational progress shows both installed and operational data center capacity rising, with additional megawatts under firm contract scheduled for phased delivery. The company indicated active engagement with Middle Eastern clients, which may be driving incremental demand for data center and network services in India.
Management is not providing specific EBITDA per megawatt guidance for modular liquid cooling deployments but noted higher capital intensity may improve returns for these sites.
Cash discipline and a focus on “cost competitiveness, cash flow optimization and fiscal discipline” are being emphasized as expansion intensifies.
Company expects ongoing quarterly margin improvement in data center services, aiming for breakeven within two years according to segment leadership.
The upcoming IPO includes a primary capital raise and a partial exit for Kotak, the growth capital partner, with specifics publicly disclosed in the DRHP.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
SDWAN
: Software-Defined Wide Area Network — a virtualized network architecture that enables centralized, efficient, and secure management of wide-area networking.
DRHP
: Draft Red Herring Prospectus — a preliminary registration document for an IPO in Indian capital markets, detailing offer structure and disclosure requirements.
Colocation
: A data center service where enterprises rent space, power, and cooling to house their servers and hardware alongside other clients in a facility managed by the provider.
